summary.name: Automation (Wikipedia article)
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia overview of automation: the use of technologies such as mechanical, electrical, electronic and computer systems to reduce human intervention in processes.
use_cases: Learning the history of automation and control systems
Understanding feedback control and the automatic control loop
Reviewing advantages and disadvantages of automating processes
Studying the paradox of automation and operator roles
summary.what_it_does: The article defines automation as technology that reduces human intervention by predetermining decision criteria and actions, implemented through mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, electrical, electronic and computer means. It traces the history of automatic control from ancient water clocks and feedback regulators through the Industrial Revolution, relay logic, PLCs, and CNC machine tools. It covers significant applications such as telephone switching, steel rolling, and chemical process control. It also discusses advantages, disadvantages, limitations, the paradox of automation, and the societal and employment impact of automation, citing several studies.
notable: Covers the history of automatic control from ancient feedback devices to modern PLCs and CNC
Discusses the paradox of automation and Bainbridge's 'Ironies of Automation'
Includes evidence on automation's effects on jobs in developed and developing economies
caveats: This is an encyclopedia article, not a software tool; it is listed on awesome-selfhosted only as a reference under 'Automation'
The page notes its current limitations section needs updating (April 2026)
